note: Every administrator and portal browser route, the application operations it performs, and how an agent performs the same work. An equivalent operation names the application service method the browser handler calls and the REST operation ids, CLI command actions and MCP tools that call it with the same authorization, revisions, idempotency, audit and refusals; a surface that withholds it carries a reason from surface_exemption_reasons. A browser-only operation carries a reason from browser_only_reasons. composition marks an equivalence reached by composing the listed operations. tools/verify-browser-machine-parity.php (composer machine:parity) fails on an unrecorded route, a stale entry, an unknown machine operation or service, or any gap. An equivalent operation whose machine surfaces authorize with less assurance than the browser carries an assurance_gap naming both sides and its decision status; the architecture suite pins that list, so it cannot grow silently.

machine_contracts.rest: The current generation named by api/openapi/generations.json

browser_only_reasons.authentication: The sign-in and sign-out forms and the browser session cookie. Machine callers authenticate with site-bound bearer or stdio tokens on every call.
browser_only_reasons.human-credential: The signed-in human's own password and second factor: change, enroll, confirm, challenge and recovery codes. A machine credential is a token, and MCP never accepts an authentication secret.
browser_only_reasons.session-context: Selecting the organization and workspace a browser session acts in. A machine credential is bound to its scope when it is issued.
browser_only_reasons.human-decision: A maker-checker decision or a change the application service gates on a fresh single-use human step-up proof bound to a browser session. A machine actor may request or cancel but never decide.
browser_only_reasons.presentation-preference: Per-user layout preferences of the browser interface; no application data changes.
browser_only_reasons.navigation: A landing page of links and counts; machine_readable_via names the operations that read the same data.
browser_only_reasons.html-presentation: An HTML-only step (a picker, a confirmation or form re-render, a component gallery) over data machine callers read through machine_readable_via; nothing is written.
browser_only_reasons.refusal-only: A route registered only so a misdirected submission is refused.
browser_only_reasons.studio-preview: The Studio preview document, its stylesheet and the preview port that renders a draft into the sandboxed frame.
browser_only_reasons.studio-shell: Studio shell affordances with no application effect: interface strings, the session permission projection, crash-recovery snapshots of unsaved editor state and client telemetry.
browser_only_reasons.transfer-protocol: A leg of the browser's granted direct-binary upload handshake. The application effect is the accepted asset, which machine_readable_via creates in one call.
browser_only_reasons.human-step-up: Requires an interactive human step-up proof. The browser demands a fresh, payload-bound, single-use second-factor proof for the change, and no machine credential can carry an equivalent proof that is bound to the operation payload, short-lived and not self-issued, so every machine surface refuses the operation.

surface_exemption_reasons.mcp-credential-boundary: MCP never accepts an authentication secret and never returns a newly issued credential (docs/mcp.md); REST and the protected console carry the secret.
surface_exemption_reasons.mcp-authority-boundary: MCP never widens authority: role assignment, capability grants and extension package installation need controls a model-tool surface does not carry (docs/mcp.md). Authority-reducing counterparts are published.
surface_exemption_reasons.mcp-password-reproof: The operation re-proves the caller's current password, which MCP cannot carry; a tool would always fail closed (docs/mcp.md).
surface_exemption_reasons.mcp-human-step-up: The browser gates the change on an interactive human step-up proof that no machine credential can carry, so MCP does not publish it (docs/mcp.md).

Resets another account's password. The browser demands a payload-bound step-up proof; REST, the console and MCP publish no equivalent and AccessControlService refuses a human context without a consumed proof (StepUpRejected).
